documents.title: Notice: Riverbend Museum temporary closure for roof maintenance
paragraphs: Notice issued 20 October 2026 by the Kestrel Bay Museums Trust.
The Riverbend Museum of Maritime History will close temporarily from Monday 26 October 2026 to Monday 2 November 2026 so that contractors can replace the roof membrane above the east gallery.
The museum will reopen to visitors on Tuesday 3 November 2026 at 10:00. Opening hours after reopening are unchanged: 10:00 to 18:00, Tuesday to Sunday.
Ticket prices are unchanged after the reopening. Adult entry remains 120 rupees; children under 12 enter free, as before.
Annual pass holders will have their passes extended by eight days to cover the closure period.
This is a temporary closure for maintenance. The museum is not closing permanently, and no collections are being moved.
For enquiries, contact the visitor desk of the Kestrel Bay Museums Trust.

documents.title: Riverbend Museum to close for a week for roof repairs
paragraphs: The Riverbend Museum of Maritime History will shut its doors for a little over a week from 26 October while its east gallery roof is replaced, the Kestrel Bay Museums Trust said in a notice on Tuesday.
The trust said the museum would reopen on 3 November at 10 am and that ticket prices would not change.

Regular visitors told the Kestrel Bay Times they were relieved the work would be quick. "I was worried when I saw the scaffolding, but a week is fine," said Meera Joshi, a retired teacher who visits every month.
The roof above the east gallery last underwent major work in 2009.

documents.title: Riverbend Museum closes for roof works, reopens 3 November
paragraphs: KESTREL BAY (Coastal Wire) — The Riverbend Museum of Maritime History will close from 26 October to 2 November for roof maintenance, according to a notice from the Kestrel Bay Museums Trust.
The museum is scheduled to reopen on Tuesday 3 November at 10:00, the notice said. Contractors will replace the roof membrane above the east gallery during the closure.
Ticket prices and opening hours will stay the same after the reopening, and annual passes will be extended by eight days.
The museum, which opened in 1987, draws about 140,000 visitors a year.

documents.title: Harbor Line metro stations shut after heavy flooding
paragraphs: Four stations on the Harbor Line metro were shut on Wednesday 14 August 2019 after overnight rain flooded the underground concourses at Dockside and Lighthouse Road.
Kestrel Bay Transit said trains would run only between Central and Fisher Market until the water was pumped out. Services were fully restored on 16 August 2019.
The city recorded 212 mm of rain in 24 hours, the highest August total in two decades.

documents.title: Harbor Line — route and stations
paragraphs: The Harbor Line metro runs between Central and Lighthouse Road with nine stations, including Dockside and Fisher Market.
Flood barriers were installed at Dockside and Lighthouse Road stations in 2021 after the 2019 flooding.
Planned service changes are announced on this page at least 48 hours in advance.

documents.title: Applications open for the 2026 merit scholarship
paragraphs: Students in classes 11 and 12 at Kestrel Bay public schools can apply for the 2026 merit scholarship until 30 November.
The scholarship covers tuition fees for one year. Applications are made through school principals; the department never asks students to forward messages or share personal details on social media.

documents.title: Council adopts Vision 2040 plan
paragraphs: Kestrel Bay city council on Thursday adopted its Vision 2040 plan, which sets goals for housing, public transport and green space over the next fourteen years.
The mayor said she hoped the plan would make Kestrel Bay "one of the most liveable cities in the region". Opposition councillors called the targets unrealistic.
The plan includes 40,000 new homes and two new metro lines, subject to funding.

documents.title: Weekly drinking water quality results, 19–25 October 2026
paragraphs: The Kestrel Bay Water Board tested 214 tap water samples from all six supply zones between 19 and 25 October 2026.
Lead was below the laboratory detection limit of 1 microgram per litre in all 214 samples. The national safety limit is 10 micrograms per litre.
Results are published every Tuesday. Residents can request a free home test through the Water Board helpline.
